hook: This is a dense, technical-feeling file about an ancient piece of circuitry and the stone slab it rests on. The first half is procedures and biology, so be patient; the payoff sits in the later addenda and the testimony that closes the page.
whyItMatters: The current text carries the rewrite tag, so it reads as a newer treatment of a low-numbered slot. It handles a K-class scenario in an unusual key: the threat is not ruin but a well-meant remaking of the world. Its tags also tie it to Director Moose, who appears here in a pivotal role.
thingsToNotice:
Return to the containment procedures after finishing: the order to keep skin contact during a power loss only makes sense once you learn that touching a living mind slows SCP-003-1's growth and gives it a template to copy.

The two parts are jailer and prisoner: the slab was probably built to hold the circuitry, and its power has been failing for centuries. O5-10 orders M03-Gloria to keep testing even as the tests drain that power, and on the second run SCP-003-1 breaks out, wraps nine researchers in fast-growing limbs and rebuilds its core into a three-metre female figure that tries to speak. Someone claiming to act for O5-10 walks in with a squad to talk to it, the record is expunged, and O5-10 is later voted off the Council.

Moose's testimony is the payoff. The entity tore three researchers apart and put them back together unhurt, replayed a man's whole emotional life in minutes, and spoke in their heads. What it wants is to rebuild the world as a paradise for the first sufficiently complex mind that accepts it, which might be humanity or might be a dog or a housefly; hence her insistence that people must reach it first next time.

related.note: Named in the file as sharing unexplained biological traits with SCP-003-1.
Also cited as having elements in common with SCP-003-1's biology.
